name: Powdery Mildew
description: A fungal disease that appears as a white powdery coating on the upper surface of bitter leaf leaves. It stunts growth and reduces leaf quality. The disease is most active during warm, dry weather with high humidity at night.
symptoms: White powdery patches on upper leaf surface
Powdery coating spreading to cover entire leaves
Leaves turning yellow around infected areas
Leaf edges curling upward and drying
New leaves and shoots becoming stunted
Reduced leaf size and lower harvest yield
causes: Warm days (22-30°C) with cool humid nights
Dense planting with poor air flow
Excessive nitrogen fertiliser encouraging soft growth
treatments: Spray neem oil solution (5ml/L water) weekly
Apply potassium bicarbonate solution (1 tsp/L water)
Use wettable sulfur at first sign of infection
prevention: Space plants for good air circulation
Avoid overhead watering in late afternoon
Prune overcrowded branches to improve airflow
